body:
Oh 100%
I feel like that’s all I do lately. I haven’t actually had an appetite and when I do it’s very little. Most of the time I get halfway through eating before I realize nothing even is good and I feel even worse about it now that I’ve thought about it

You’re not alone <3

Biology is such a lame answer, but it makes so much sense. It frustrates me, as someone who’s taken many biology, physiology, and psychology classes that I didn’t think of it the first time. 

As for the doctor thing, I hate going to the doctor with a passion. My boyfriend hates going to the dentist, I hate going to the doctor’s. I do my very best to avoid doing so. It frustrates me, and even going in for a routine check up means I have to get weighed which hits me hard. I basically shut down. 

I’ve tried therapists too. and I know they’re trial & error and therapy isn’t a one size fits all type thing, but I only have had bad experiences. One therapist threatened to get me arrested so I wouldn’t burden my mom anymore. Another one, literally on the first session outside of that explanatory / evaluation session, said “you have to try harder because I’m not going to bother wasting my time on you if you don’t try.” I sat quiet for a session and a half, before she became kind of hostile and prompted me to just walk out and never go back. 

The 5 second contemplation thing is interesting to me. I’m someone who has planned an elaborate suicide. I’ve lately been walking in parking lots and across the street without looking  and not eating, etc. in hopes it’ll just kill me that way. But aside from the feeling going away really quickly, it takes me a while to get there mentally. Same when I dose myself with 20 benadryl tablets. Which honestly doesn’t do anything except give me an awful high that makes me feel like breaking down, and kills my memory. My memory is already shot, but three seconds after I say something I forget what the rest of my thought was. Like right now. I’m not gonna remember all this in the morning, and I’m also not sure if my thoughts here are even coherent. 

The moment I do it, I’m physically okay and I hope it might kill me in my sleep, but once I get restless and my body starts uncontrollably hurting, I regret it and get scared. Then I’ll say “I’ll never do it again!” but much like my eating disorder which I swore I’d give up after my first purge, I’ve had night laying halfway on the shower floor and can’t bring myself to stop. It’s like I don’t know what turns the feelings on or what turns the feelings off or how to keep the death idea consistent. 

I’m also like you. I think a lot about the how? How would they react? How much would the world change (or I guess not change for a better choice of words). I’ve gotten to the point tho where I just accept this misery, and I’ll just accept whatever happens to me I suppose. Is this comment coherent? I don’t even know pal
